title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is cutting out the image of Gamma_Q inside Out(SL(2,Z)^), where SL(2,Z)^ is the profinite completion, viewed as the geometric fundamental group of the stack M_{1,1} over Q-bar. The previous page showed two constraints. (i) The outer action of Gamma_Q on SL(2,Z-hat) factors through the multiquadratic quotient Gamma -> Z-hat*/Z-hat*^2. (ii) The image subgroup must preserve the kernel of SL(2,Z)^ -> SL(2,Z-hat).

This page adds a sharper constraint coming from the cusp, the point at infinity of M_{1,1,Q}.

Step 1 (eq. 8). The cusp gives an outer class of homomorphisms T = T_infty(Q-bar_0) -> SL(2,Z)^. Here T, isomorphic to Z-hat(1), is the local (inertia) fundamental group of a punctured neighbourhood of the cusp.

Step 2 (eq. 9). Composed with the map to SL(2,Z-hat), the image of T is, up to conjugacy, the unipotent subgroup of matrices (1 0; n 1), n in Z-hat, i.e. the closure of the cusp stabiliser generated by the parabolic element.

Step 3 (eq. 10). Since the cusp is Q-rational, Gamma_Q respects this outer homomorphism. Hence Gamma acts on T, giving a character Gamma -> Aut(T) = Z-hat*, which is the cyclotomic character.

Step 4 (generalisation). Let u be any outer automorphism of SL(2,Z)^ (or of SL(2,Z-hat)) that preserves the conjugacy class of the image of T. Grothendieck asserts there is a unique chi(u) in Aut(T) = Z-hat* making the square T -> SL(2,Z)^ commute, with chi(u) on the left and u on the right (diagram 11, next page).

Step 5 (purpose, completed on the next page). This defines a subgroup of Out(SL(2,Z)^) carrying a 'cyclotomic character' chi. It is an elliptic analogue of the chi: GT-hat -> Z-hat* of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group. Gamma_Q lies in it, together with the further compatibility that the induced outer action on SL(2,Z-hat) goes through chi followed by reduction modulo squares.

This is a step in the programme of describing Gamma_Q combinatorially as a subgroup of Out of the profinite Teichmüller groups. The margin note 'joindre la justification' shows the existence and uniqueness of chi(u) is left unproved here.
errors: Uniqueness of chi(u) needs two facts not justified on the page. First, T -> SL(2,Z)^ must be injective. Second, the normalizer of the image of T must act trivially on T (it should be ±T, i.e. the cusp subgroup is self-normalizing up to the centre). Both are true but nontrivial (commensurable terminality of cusp/inertia subgroups, later proved e.g. by Nakamura/Mochizuki-type arguments). The margin 'joindre la justification' acknowledges the gap.

In the variant with SL(2,Z-hat) ('ou semblable de SL(2,Z-hat)'), uniqueness fails. The normalizer of the unipotent subgroup contains diagonal matrices diag(a, a^{-1}), which act on n by multiplication by a^{±2}. So chi(u) is only determined modulo Z-hat*^2. This is consistent with the next page, where only the class in Z-hat*/Z-hat*^2 appears for SL(2,Z-hat). The claim 'unique' is correct only for SL(2,Z)^.

ideas.what: Cusp at infinity of M_{1,1} gives an outer homomorphism from the local inertia group T ≅ Z-hat(1) into SL(2,Z)^, with unipotent image in SL(2,Z-hat)
ideas.modern_name: cusp/tangential inertia subgroup of the profinite modular group
ideas.where_published: related discussion of M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z)^ in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Galois action on cusp inertia is via the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on inertia at a rational cusp = cyclotomic character

ideas.what: Extending chi to all outer automorphisms of SL(2,Z)^ preserving the cusp conjugacy class, giving a 'cyclotomic character' on a combinatorially defined subgroup of Out(SL(2,Z)^) containing Gamma_Q
ideas.modern_name: chi: GT-type group -> Z-hat*; cusp-preserving outer automorphism groups of profinite modular groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps for the genus-0 GT analogue; elliptic versions by Nakamura, Enriquez
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the idea of describing Gamma_Q via automorphisms of the Teichmüller tower, without this explicit construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit 'elliptic' GT-type subgroup of Out(SL(2,Z)^). It is defined by preserving the cusp class (with induced chi), normalizing the congruence kernel, and inducing the outer action on SL(2,Z-hat) through chi mod squares. He leaves its justification and its comparison with Gamma_Q open. Close analogues exist in the later literature (Nakamura's work on profinite SL(2,Z), Enriquez's elliptic GT), so the novelty is mainly historical priority.
missed.quote: pour tout automorphisme extérieur u de Sl(2,Z)^ ... qui invarie la classe des conjugaisons de l'image de (8) ... il existe un χ(u) ∈ Aut(T) ≃ Ẑ* unique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's early, explicit formulation of a 'one-cusp' GT-type condition for M_{1,1}. This predates or parallels Drinfeld/Ihara/Nakamura; of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard facts (cusp inertia, cyclotomic action), used to define a GT-like character on outer automorphisms. The idea is anticipated in the Esquisse and developed later by others; there is a small gap regarding uniqueness for SL(2,Z-hat).
transcription_corrections: 'vu une opération' is more likely 'd'où une opération'.
'ǔ' in 'automorphisme extérieur ǔ' is probably just 'u'.
'à conj. près envers' is likely a garbled insertion; the readable sense is 'dont l'image dans Sl(2,Ẑ) est (à conj. près) un sous-groupe unipotent'.
Last lines: 'commutativité dans' (diagram on next page).
